original_value: This article reports the results of the study related to emotion recognition by using eye-tracking. Emotions were evoked by presenting a dynamic movie material in the form of 21 video fragments. Eye-tracking signals recorded from 30 participants were used to calculate 18 features associated with eye movements (fixations and saccades) and pupil diameter. To ensure that the features were related to emotions, we investigated the influence of luminance and the dynamics of the presented movies. Three classes of emotions were considered: high arousal and low valence, low arousal and moderate valence, and high arousal and high valence. A maximum of 80% classification accuracy was obtained using the support vector machine (SVM) classifier and leave-one-subject-out validation method.

result.paraphrase: This article presents the results of a study on emotion recognition using eye tracking. Emotions were elicited by showing dynamic movie content in 21 video fragments. Eye-tracking data from 30 participants were used to compute 18 features related to eye movements, including fixations and saccades, as well as pupil diameter. To verify that the features were tied to emotions, the effects of luminance and the movies’ dynamics were examined. Three emotion classes were analyzed: high arousal with low valence, low arousal with moderate valence, and high arousal with high valence. Using an SVM classifier with leave-one-subject-out validation, a maximum classification accuracy of 80% was achieved.
